name: relative_neighborhood_graph (relative neighborhood graph of a spatial point set)

benchmarks.note: deterministic LCG scatter in the unit square. The kernel enumerates all O(n^2) candidate pairs and runs an O(n) empty-lune test per pair, so cost is cubic in the point count: 25->100 (4x points) is ~18x time, 100->200 (2x points) is ~4.3x time, both tracking the n^3 expectation. Faster than the Gabriel kernel at equal n: the open-lune predicate rejects on the first endpoint test, so most pairs short-circuit early

k x k triangular lattice (k in 5,10,14): every edge has a third lattice point exactly equidistant, so the open-lune boundary branch fires on every surviving edge. Slower than the scatter at equal n because lattice pairs survive deeper into the empty-lune loop before rejection; still cubic overall
